title: CedarBridge vendor assurance questionnaire walkthrough
summary: Redwood walked CedarBridge through the vendor assurance questionnaire focusing on SIG/CAIQ mapping, SOC 2 controls, KMS/HSM options, and audit log retention. Team agreed next steps: share security pack and SOC 2 report, schedule an evidence intake call, and confirm VPC pilot timeline.

Encryption: KMS vs HSM, customer-managed keys

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Karim (CedarBridge InfoSec), Tom Reynolds (Cloud), Priya Suresh (Procurement)
Shared links: Redwood security pack: https://redwood.example/security-pack/cedarbridge; SIG template: https://files.cedarbridge/internal/sig-template.xlsx (customer)

[00:00] Olivia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Olivia, AE on the account. Marcus will go deep on the technical answers. Aisha, Tom, Priya, thanks for the time.
[00:12] Aisha (CedarBridge): Hi all, thanks. We got the SIG v2 and a CAIQ variant from procurement. Quick objective: we want to understand what evidence you can provide vs what we need to collect. Also data residency and KMS are high priority for us.
[00:26] Marcus (Redwood): Great. I'll call out where we can provide attestation artifacts vs where we need customer artifacts. Quick note, sorry if the transcript is fuzzy — some of our notes say KV cash instead of KV cache, that happens.
[00:36] Priya: No worries. We'll try to keep questions grouped.
[00:40] Marcus: Ok, starting with SOC 2. Redwood has a current SOC 2 type II report covering security and availability, and we have an internal mapping we can share that ties the control families to SIG questions. We can provide the SOC 2 attestation as evidence; however, for controls that require customer-side configuration, like SSO/SAML or VPC isolation, we need screenshots or configs from CedarBridge.
[01:05] Aisha: When you say SSO/SAML, do you support customer-managed IdP with SCIM user provisioning and SAML 2.0? We need RBAC integration with our existing group mappings.
[01:18] Marcus: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Role-based access controls map to SAML attributes or SCIM groups. There are a few caveats: if you want enforcement inside Private on-prem deployments, there is a light agent for RBAC sync — for Redwood hosted we integrate via SAML and pipeline the group claims. We can share an implementation guide with attribute mappings.
[01:40] Tom: For Private VPC, how does key management work? We need KMS where keys are customer-managed — ideally HSM-backed.
[01:48] Marcus: Good question. Two paths: Hosted dedicated/private with customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS with key policy restricting Redwood), or an HSM option for Private installations. For VPC deployments we can configure BYOK with an external HSM or cloud KMS. We rotate keys by default every 90 days, but for BYOK the rotation schedule is up to the customer; Redwood supports import and rotation hooks. We'll include our KMS/HSM diagram in the security pack.
[02:13] Aisha: Do you store any unencrypted copies of customer data in logs or traces? Audit log retention is a concern.
[02:20] Marcus: We encrypt logs at rest. Application-level traces redact PII by default; however some debug traces may capture prompts depending on configuration. By default hosted retention for logs is 90 days, but for Dedicated and Private you control retention and export. We can set up a pipeline to forward logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and keep tamper-evident storage. Also note, our audit logs include token-level attribution and model invocation metadata but not raw customer plaintext by default — unless you opt-in to store request bodies for evaluation.
[02:53] Priya: On the SIG, there are several items asking for evidence of encryption in transit and at rest, HSM attestations, and KMS key policies. How granular is the evidence you can provide?
[03:05] Olivia: We'll provide the SOC 2 report, our crypto architecture diagram, KMS key policy examples, and a redacted HSM attestation where allowed. Some vendor HSM providers don't allow full attestation disclosure but we can provide vendor statements and procedural evidence.
[03:23] Aisha: Ok. For data residency, we need to pin production traffic to EU regions. Is there an SLA for region pinning and are backups replicated across regions?
[03:34] Marcus: You can pin to specific regions. For Hosted we have region selection per-account; backups can be configured either single-region or cross-region replication depending on your contract. For full on-prem Private deployments data doesn't leave your network unless you opt into cross-region backups. We'll call out options in the documentation.
[03:55] Tom: Can we get an export of audit logs for the last 365 days for the POC?
[04:00] Marcus: For Dedicated/Priavte we can export historical logs as long as they're retained. Hosted standard retention may be shorter, but we can agree to an extended retention as part of a pilot. We'll note that as an action item.
[04:12] Priya: Procurement will need to confirm the timelines for extended retention since it may affect pricing.
[04:17] Olivia: Totally, we'll provide a pricing appendix with options for retention and HSM add-ons.
[04:22] Aisha: On network controls, do you have SOC2 evidence for segmentation between customers and tenant isolation? There's a SIG question about logical separation.
[04:31] Marcus: We use tenant-level isolation at the application and storage layers. For Dedicated it's physically isolated pools; for hosted multi-tenant, we have strict namespace and RBAC isolation plus encryption per tenant. We'll link the network diagrams and control descriptions in the pack.
[04:46] Aisha: A few SIG items ask for business continuity and disaster recovery evidence, like RTO/RPO numbers.
[04:52] Marcus: Our DR plan is in the security pack — typical RTO targets for hosted API are sub-5 minutes for failover of control plane components and RPO depends on replication config; standard is 1 hour. For Dedicated we can negotiate stricter RTO/RPO in the contract.
[05:10] Tom: On the technical deep dive, we want to run a small perf benchmark — can Redwood provide a perf baseline with AES GCM encryption enabled and KV cache on?
[05:18] Marcus: Yes, we'll produce a perf baseline for the model type you expect to use, with encryption and cache settings. We'll include token latency numbers at 8k context and typical batching.
[05:29] Aisha: Are there any controls where you can't provide evidence because it's customer responsibility? We need a clear split.
[05:36] Marcus: Yes — identity and access controls for your Okta tenant, your network firewall configs, and your internal change management evidence are customer responsibilities. We can provide sample templates for evidence collection and a checklist that maps each SIG question to either Redwood-provided artifacts or customer-provided artifacts.
[05:52] Olivia: We'll send that checklist as a spreadsheet mapping each SIG item to owner and evidence type. That usually speeds up reviews.
[05:59] Priya: That spreadsheet would be helpful. Procurement also needs the signed subprocessor list.
[06:05] Marcus: We maintain an updated subprocessor list and can provide a redacted copy or legal version under NDA.
[06:11] Aisha: Auditability — do you provide WORM storage or tamper-evident logs? We need to show chain of custody for certain requests.
[06:20] Marcus: We can deliver immutable snapshots for logs (WORM) to object storage and provide checksums for integrity. For the hosted option, those exports can be pushed to your S3 bucket with object lock enabled.
[06:33] Tom: For encryption key controls, is there a separation of duties between ops engineers and key admins? We have strict policies.
[06:40] Marcus: Yes, role separation is possible. Access to KMS keys is controlled by IAM and KMS key policies — ops have operational keys for runtime but can't download key material if you're using BYOK with HSM. We'll include an RBAC matrix.
[06:55] Aisha: Any automated evidence workflows? For our security team, manual upload is painful.
[07:01] Marcus: We have an evidence portal for customers on Dedicated/Private where you can upload and tag evidence items; we also accept S3 bucket ingestion with prefixed paths. For high-volume customers we can set up an API to push evidence items and metadata.
[07:15] Priya: That API would help procurement. We'll need doc on required naming conventions.
[07:19] Olivia: We'll include the evidence API spec link in the security pack.
[07:24] [Brief cross-talk, someone drops microphone]
[07:30] Aisha: A few SIG questions around encryption algorithms, are you using RSA or ECC for key wrapping? Any PQ crypto?
[07:38] Marcus: We currently use AES-256-GCM for data encryption at rest, and keys are wrapped with RSA-3072 or RSA-4096 on partner HSMs. We don't have production PQC yet, but it's on the roadmap — we'll note that in the response where we mark it as roadmap.
[07:55] Priya: Procurement wants explicit language on indemnity for data breach and third-party subprocessors. Is that something you can outline now or in the contract addendum?
[08:03] Olivia: We handle indemnity and subprocessors in the contract addendum; procurement will get our standard terms, and for enterprise deals we can negotiate limited indemnity language. We'll attach the subprocessor addendum.
[08:15] Tom: About logs again, are request bodies ever stored in plaintext backups? You mentioned config changes can cause debug traces to contain prompts.
[08:24] Marcus: By default we avoid storing raw request bodies for hosted customers. For debugging during the POC, if you opt-in to session recording, we can collect request bodies with consent and those artifacts are encrypted and labeled. We'll provide redaction guidance for PII.
[08:40] Aisha: On SSO, do you support Just-In-Time provisioning?
[08:44] Marcus: SCIM gives near real-time provisioning and deprovisioning; we also support JIT for SAML attribute-based provisioning.
[08:52] Priya: For the SIG spreadsheet, we will mark around 30 controls as high priority for CedarBridge — mostly key management, logs, and region pinning. Can we get a quick scoring from Redwood on high-risk items?
[09:02] Olivia: Yes, Marcus can provide risk flags per SIG item (Low/Medium/High) based on typical enterprise posture.
[09:09] Marcus: I'll annotate the spreadsheet with recommended mitigations and whether Redwood or the customer owns the control.
[09:16] Aisha: Evidence delivery timeline — if we need 90 days' worth of audit logs and a copy of SOC2, what does the turnaround look like?
[09:24] Marcus: SOC2 is immediate — we'll share the attestation by the 23rd. Audit log exports depend on retention: for hosted with default retention we may need to spin up an export and that could take 2–3 business days for the POC. For Dedicated it's faster.
[09:38] Olivia: I'll confirm the SOC2 availability and send it with the security pack.
[09:42] Tom: Any red flags with the SIG? Anything you anticipate the vendor risk team will push back on?
[09:48] Marcus: The common pushback items are request body storage and key custody. If CedarBridge requires customer-managed keys exclusively and WORM logs with 7-year retention, that will push to a Dedicated/Private solution and will affect pricing. We'll flag those as high. Otherwise standard SOC2 and KMS policies satisfy many SIG questions.
[10:06] Priya: Ok that's helpful. Procurement will want a cost delta for BYOK + extended retention + HSM.
[10:12] Olivia: We'll add a pricing appendix to the pack with line items.
[10:18] Aisha: One of our compliance folks asked about continuous monitoring — do you have a feed for vulnerability scans or pen test results?
[10:26] Marcus: We publish summary results and issue tracker metrics; full penetration test reports are provided under NDA. We also publish a monthly security bulletin.
[10:35] Priya: Great. On the evidence portal, can we get scoped access for reviewers? We don't want all contractors to see everything.
[10:42] Marcus: Yes, role-based access on the portal is supported; you can create reviewer roles with read-only access to tagged evidence.
[10:49] Olivia: Let's summarize next steps so procurement and security are aligned.
[10:53] Olivia: Action items: I'll send the security pack + SOC2 attestation; Marcus will annotate the SIG spreadsheet and prepare a VPC pilot checklist and perf baseline; CedarBridge will flag priority SIG items and share network diagrams. We'll schedule the evidence intake meeting for the first week of March.
[11:10] Aisha: Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood side for the March window?
[11:14] Marcus: No blockers — we have capacity for a pilot in early March.
[11:19] Tom: One last question — do you support tenant-level encryption with customer KMS in hosted mode or only for dedicated/private?
[11:26] Marcus: We support tenant keys in hosted mode via customer-managed KMS and key policies in the cloud provider; however full HSM-backed keys with sealed import are recommended for Dedicated/Private if you need hardware separation.
[11:40] Priya: Thanks, that's clear. Procurement will wait for the pricing appendix.
[11:44] Olivia: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the pack and SOC2 by Monday. If anything urgent, ping me directly.
[11:52] Aisha: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
